CORRECTION - I ASSERTED THAT THREE OF SL-032's FOUR ROWS HAD WRONG SIZING. IT WAS TWO. The claim was mine, it was false, and I propagated it into SIX artifacts across one day before a sweep caught it while preparing the resume prompt.

THE TRUTH, verified against the rows rather than recollection. DW-040's sizing was WRONG: it said 'only the gesture' and the work needed a backend change - the operation was a SWAP, indistinguishable from a move at plus-or-minus one and wrong for any longer drag - plus a new addressing mode. DW-038's was WRONG: it said 'draw the chart to a canvas... NOT blocked on anything' and there is no canvas (OQ-022 Approved, ADR-0022 removed the chart library) and it was blocked on two real things. DW-061's was RIGHT: its own row sized it as 'one i18n key pair plus a breakpoint-guarded banner; small' and a CSS-only notice is exactly what shipped. DW-032's was RIGHT: every clause held when the code was read. TWO WRONG, TWO RIGHT.

WHERE IT CAME FROM, because the mechanism is the transferable part. prm-next carried a TRUE sentence - 'read the code before believing a row's sizing - that habit PAID three times in this slice' - which counts two catches plus one confirmation. I read 'paid three times' and wrote 'three were wrong'. A count of what an instrument DID is not a count of what it FOUND, and the two differ by exactly the confirmations. This is LL-015's shape one level up: not a scan whose scope was wrong, but a NUMBER whose subject was wrong, carried into prose where no gate can see it.

THE SIX ARTIFACTS, all corrected or superseded. DW-032's row and SL-032's objective (both re-upserted; each diff verified against a captured pre-image so only the intended sentences changed). SL-033's objective, which was carrying it forward as the standing warning for eight unbuilt rows - the worst of the six, because it was instruction rather than history. prm-next's new section 6 head. The memory topic file wbs234-reclassify.md. And two progress entries, PE-583 and PE-591, which are APPEND-ONLY and are corrected by this entry rather than edited - PE-583 names DW-061, DW-040 and DW-038 as 'all three wrong', and PE-591 repeats 'Three of SL-032's four'.

⚠⚠ SL-032's OBJECTIVE ALSO CARRIED THE HEADLINE-VERSUS-ENUMERATION MISMATCH THIS SESSION FILED AGAINST SOMEONE ELSE. Its heading said THREE OF THE FOUR ROWS' SIZINGS WERE WRONG and the paragraph beneath it only ever enumerated TWO. That is precisely the defect I recorded against DEF-104 hours earlier - a row whose headline and its own list disagree, with nothing in the package comparing them. Writing that finding down did not stop me reproducing it.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE, and it is the part worth keeping: read the code before believing a row's sizing. The habit is not weakened by the correction - it caught DW-040 and DW-038, and it CONFIRMED DW-061 and DW-032, which is what a working check looks like. Two of SL-033's eight rows already carry corrections in their own text (DW-037's scheduled date is not on the Topics side; DW-063's Stream.Create still has no caller), so the warning stands with an accurate number behind it.

HOW IT WAS FOUND: preparing prm-next for a fresh session, by re-reading the file end to end as its own preamble instructs, and noticing that the file said TWO where I had been saying THREE. The prompt was right and I was wrong. ⚠ The file's instruction to re-verify it before handing it on is what surfaced this; the mechanical id-and-status pass had already run clean over all 170 identifiers and could not see it, exactly as the tenth fix predicted.

entry: LESSON CONFIRMED: LL-016 (confirmed_by Operator) — operator_confirm attested

OPERATOR INTERVIEW, 2026-08-23 (later), run at the operator's request immediately after the SL-033 resume was prepared and pushed. Four questions, each carrying the cited records' own text inline rather than their identifiers (LL-011). Recorded as DEC-072 d1-d4 and applied by SC-032, now Merged. TWO OF THE FOUR ANSWERS OVERRODE MY RECOMMENDATION and are recorded as overrides with the reasoning against preserved, following the DEC-071 d3 precedent rather than erasing the disagreement. d1, THE DEPENDABOT QUEUE: thirteen pull requests are open against a live production deployment, the oldest dating to 2026-07-16, three of them major-version bumps - mssql/server 2022-latest to 2025-latest, typescript 6.0.3 to 7.0.2 and vitest 3.2.6 to 4.1.10. I recommended merging the routine set and carrying the three majors; the operator's answer was sweep everything, majors included. DW-078 carries the work AND the shape the chosen option specified - a dedicated batch with the full e2e leg per risky bump, and a fresh-volume verification for the mssql bump before it approaches the dev stack's five populated volumes, because SQL Server keeps the volume's original SA password and the recorded recovery for a failed recreate destroys all five. THE FIRST THING THE ROW GETS RIGHT IS THAT THIS IS NOT AN NFR-051 BREACH: that requirement is Implemented and requires Dependabot to be CONFIGURED TO ALERT, which it demonstrably is - thirteen open alerts are the requirement working. Nothing in the register obliges anyone to act on an alert, so the gap is real and uncovered rather than a violation, and I swept the registers by keyword before raising it precisely because LL-005 exists. d2, AND THIS IS THE ONE I WOULD NOT HAVE FOUND WITHOUT READING THE ROW'S OWN WORDS: DW-071's activation trigger carries TWO clauses and only the second was parked by DEC-071 d4. The first reads whenever a new route ships - that is the moment the ratio gets worse, and the moment it is cheapest to add the route to the sweep. SL-033 ships three new user-visible surfaces, so by the row's own text the clause fires INSIDE the slice, and the operator judged that it had. THE SUMMARY OF A ROW HAD DROPPED HALF OF WHAT THE ROW SAID, which is DEC-064 d2's failure inverted: there an instruction never reached a row, here the row's own words carried an obligation the label over it had lost. DW-071 is Activated; each SL-033 item that ships a surface adds its route to e2e/rtl-a11y.spec.ts in the same batch and says so in its own acceptance criterion. The live axe sweep currently visits three of fifty-two routes, so shipping three more surfaces untouched would have worsened a ratio the register already records. d3, LL-016 Approved and PINNED in one step, the operator having read the exact statement in the interview with refine-first available and not taken - the statement is stored byte-identical to what they read, because approved lessons are immutable here. d4, THE NFR-018 EVIDENCE PACK: I recommended leaving it alone as externally blocked with no trigger fired; the operator chose to prepare it now. DW-079 carries it and states twice, in its own words, that it does NOT close NFR-018 and that no acceptance criterion may be written from it, since only an external assessor's report can evidence the requirement and an AC ahead of that report would hold readiness false forever. NOTHING DEC-071 SETTLED THIS MORNING WAS RE-RAISED. MECHANISM LEARNED AND WORTH KEEPING: scope_adds to a deferred-work target had never been used in this package - every prior scope_adds edge pointed at an acceptance criterion, a requirement or a slice - and the store ACCEPTS it, so the relation rules are wider than this package's practice had shown. Also confirmed by experiment rather than assumption: source_kind on deferred_work is a CHECK over brief, clarification, code and inferred, and a row using anything else rolls back the entire batch. DW-071's status change was done as a full-row replace with a sha256 pre-image taken first and verified after - its 2097-character measured title and its custom_attributes came back byte-identical, and custom_attributes was preserved by OMISSION, which is PE-585's failure shape defended against rather than merely remembered. ONE THING IS DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED AND IS THE OPERATOR'S: whether the dependency sweep runs BEFORE SL-033 or beside it. DW-078's trigger says so in as many words rather than letting a later session pick silently.

entry: DEC-073 - THE DEPENDENCY SWEEP RUNS BEFORE SL-033, SO DW-078 IS THE NEXT ACTION AND WBS-24.1 IS NOT. Operator answer to the one question DEC-072 d1 deliberately left open and DW-078's own trigger reserved to them. WBS-24.1 waits until the queue is clear. The reasoning is attribution: a TypeScript 6-to-7 major and a SQL Server 2022-to-2025 major landing underneath eight items already in flight give any later failure two candidate causes, and every SL-033 item should be built, tested and reviewed against the versions it will actually ship on. The accepted cost is that the live slice pauses for a batch, and the queue's oldest entries are already five weeks old. WHAT THIS ENTRY IS REALLY ABOUT, and it is the reusable part: ONE ANSWER FALSIFIED FOUR ARTIFACTS I HAD WRITTEN MINUTES EARLIER. DW-078's activation trigger said the ordering was undecided; DEC-072 d1 said it; the prm-next carried block said 'Ask; do not pick'; and the memory index said the same. All four were corrected in ONE pass with a grep proving no residual claim survived, rather than one at a time - which is the direct application of PE-592, where a single wrong count reached six artifacts across a day because each was fixed where it was noticed instead of being swept for. A STATEMENT THAT A QUESTION IS OPEN DECAYS EXACTLY LIKE A STATEMENT OF FACT, and it decays at the moment the question is answered - which is the moment you are least likely to go looking for it, because you are busy recording the answer. DW-078 STARTED AND STOPPED ON ITS FIRST MEASUREMENT - DEF-105. Assessing the ten in-scope pull requests before merging anything, two things came out that change how the sweep must run and one of them is a defect against an invariant.

FIRST, THE SWEEP'S OWN PREMISE. Every green in the queue is stale, and the staleness is not marginal. mergeStateStatus reads CLEAN for #139, #255, #256, #257, #258, #259 and #260, and UNSTABLE for #135, #137 and #261. The check runs behind those verdicts are dated 2026-08-13 for most, 2026-08-07 for #137 and #139, and 2026-07-17 for #135. Meanwhile main has taken the whole of SL-032 plus DEF-103 and DEF-104 since. THE SHARPEST CASE IS #139, THE typescript 6.0.3 TO 7.0.2 MAJOR, WHICH REPORTS NINE OF NINE SUCCESS FROM 2026-08-07: A GREEN CHECK CANNOT HAVE TESTED CODE THAT DID NOT EXIST WHEN IT RAN, and the drag-to-reprioritize work, the PNG chart export and the reclassify dialog all landed after that date. A compiler major green against a tree missing three features is not evidence about today's tree. CLEAN is a statement about a past run, not about merging into current main. The sweep must update each branch onto main and wait for a FRESH run before merging - DW-078's recorded shape said 'full e2e leg per risky bump' and did not say this, because nobody knew freshness was unenforced.

SECOND, WHY IT IS UNENFORCED - DEF-105, and the observable that gave it away was a status that NEVER APPEARED. Across all twelve pull requests not one reported mergeStateStatus BEHIND, and BEHIND is the status GitHub reports only when a repository requires branches to be up to date. Checking that: GET /repos/A-H-911/acmp/branches/main/protection returns 404 Branch not protected; GET /rulesets returns an empty array; GET /rules/branches/main - which reports the rules ACTUALLY applying to a branch from every mechanism, and is the check that makes this conclusive rather than a single-endpoint inference (LL-006) - also returns empty. MAIN HAS NO PROTECTION OF ANY KIND. Nothing requires a pull request, a review, or a green check before a commit lands.

THAT WOULD BE A CONFIGURATION PREFERENCE IF THE PACKAGE DID NOT ASSERT THE OPPOSITE AS FACT IN FIVE PLACES, ONE OF THEM AN INVARIANT. INV-013's enforcement column reads 'branch protection; CI; git workflow'. SEC-120: 'PR rules (enforced via branch protection): Minimum 1 approver. All required CI checks must pass before merge.' SEC-126, the flatly false one: 'All required checks enforced via branch protection; cannot merge/deploy without passing.' SEC-172 tells the operator to configure it. SEC-581 repeats the enforcement column. An invariant whose named enforcement does not exist is enforced by discipline alone, and the register describes that discipline as machinery - the manufactured-assurance shape of DEF-010, and the same family as DEF-078's healthcheck that evaluated zero checks. THE CONTROL READS GREEN BECAUSE IT IS NOT THERE TO FAIL.

IN FAIRNESS, AND THE ROW SAYS SO: the discipline HAS held. Every merge to date went through a pull request with green CI, which is why this surfaced as a documentation-versus-reality gap rather than as a bad merge. Severity is medium by the register's own calibration - DEF-100 and DEF-102 are both medium and both comparable - and the operator may judge it higher, since a false sentence in the security narrative is exactly what an ASVS assessor reads as a finding about the assurance process, which makes it DW-079's business too.

NOT MERGED, NOTHING TOUCHED. Two questions are the operator's before this proceeds: whether to configure branch protection now or carry DEF-105, and whether the sweep rebases every branch for a fresh run - the honest but slow path, one CI cycle each - or accepts stale greens for the three routine digest bumps only.

SEPARATELY, AND IT IS A NON-FINDING WORTH RECORDING BECAUSE IT COST A CHECK: a diagnostics panel reported twenty-six errors across main.tsx, ReportsPage.tsx, MobileNotice.test.tsx, Kanban.tsx and vr-reclassify.tsx. DEF-105 FIXED - BRANCH PROTECTION NOW EXISTS ON main, AND THE FIX PROVED ITSELF BY MOVING AN OBSERVABLE THAT HAD NEVER APPEARED. Operator decision in the same interview: protect main, with a bypass so the 2026-08-20 rule that package, prompt and memory writes go straight to main survives. Applied by PUT /repos/A-H-911/acmp/branches/main/protection with strict=true (branches must be up to date - this is what closes the stale-green hole the defect was found through), required contexts backend, frontend, compose, e2e, secrets, sast, trivy-fs, trivy-image and sbom, enforce_admins=false for the direct-push path, required_approving_review_count=0, required_linear_history=true, force pushes and deletions off.

THE PROOF IS NOT AN ASSERTION. Immediately before the change, no pull request in the repository reported mergeStateStatus BEHIND - that universal absence is what exposed the gap in the first place, since BEHIND is emitted only when a repository requires branches to be up to date. Immediately after, ALL TWELVE report BEHIND. The instrument went from never emitting the status to emitting it on every row, which is LL-013's discipline applied to a configuration change rather than a test: the number moved, so the control has a subject. It also establishes retroactively that all twelve pull requests were behind the whole time while six of them reported CLEAN.

TWO CONFIGURATION CHOICES WERE READ OUT OF THE SYSTEM RATHER THAN GUESSED, and both would have caused a silent failure. FIRST, 'publish' is deliberately NOT a required check: it reports SKIPPED on pull requests, and a required check that never reports leaves a pull request pending forever - A GATE THAT CANNOT BE SATISFIED IS AS BROKEN AS ONE THAT CANNOT FAIL, which is trap 31 in the other direction. SECOND, reading the three workflow trigger blocks rather than assuming they matched found an asymmetry worth recording: ci.yml's pull_request trigger ignores only *.md, but e2e.yml's and security.yml's ALSO ignore tamheed-package/** and .claude/**. So a pull request touching only package paths would skip seven of the nine required checks and hang forever. That is acceptable - package writes go straight to main and never form a pull request, and admin bypass resolves it if one ever does - but it is written into DEF-105 so a future session finding a package PR stuck reads a sentence instead of debugging CI.

RESIDUAL CARRIED AS DW-081 RATHER THAN QUIETLY CLOSED: SEC-120 states 'Minimum 1 approver (lead or peer)' and the configuration sets 0, because GitHub forbids self-approval and this is a one-human team - the clause is UNSATISFIABLE, not merely unmet, and configuring 1 would have blocked every merge this project makes. That is the DEF-096 shape, where NFR-054's 500 MB cap was unsatisfiable against a 3.62 GB image and became a carried row rather than a silent relaxation. The two honest ends are a second reviewer or a corrected sentence, and both are the operator's; the row says explicitly not to just delete the clause, because SC-024 and DEC-066 both record this operator declining to narrow a requirement rather than track the gap.

DEF-105 IS Fixed AND THE DEFECT'S OWN TITLE WAS REWRITTEN RATHER THAN PRESERVED, applying the rule recorded in PE-600 hours earlier: hash-and-verify when you must preserve, rewrite openly when you must change. Its claim was 'no branch protection exists', which is now false as a present-tense sentence, so preserving it verbatim would have been transcription risk in the service of keeping something that needed to change anyway.

DW-078 SWEEP, FIRST HALF: THREE MERGED, ONE PROVEN UNMERGEABLE, ONE PAIR REPLACED BY A COMBINED PULL REQUEST - AND FOUR OF MY OWN INSTRUMENTS FAILED IN THE PROCESS, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING.

MERGED, each on a green that actually included current main: #255 nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged digest (7bd9c7f), #257 node digest (02d84de), #259 the npm-minor-patch group of six (312762a). Each cycle was rebase, wait for a fresh run, verify every conclusion, squash-merge, sync. CI turned out to take about eight minutes rather than the twenty budgeted.

#135 mssql/server 2022-latest to 2025-latest IS NOT MERGEABLE, AND THE REASON IS NOT WHAT I FIRST SAID. Its five-week-old red was correctly distrusted - A STALE RED IS EXACTLY AS UNINFORMATIVE AS A STALE GREEN, and the whole sweep exists because of stale greens - so it was rebased and re-run. It fails identically on a fresh run against current main: SearchProvidersFtsTests, the only place any FREETEXT branch executes, dies because the CONTAINER NEVER STARTS. The message is '/opt/mssql/bin/sqlservr: error while loading shared libraries: liblber-2.5.so.0: cannot open shared object file', exit code 127. THE SQL SERVER BINARY ITSELF WILL NOT BOOT IN THAT IMAGE. My first reading of the older log blamed Testcontainers' sqlcmd path discovery, because the stack trace's nearest frame is FindSqlCmdFilePathAsync - and that frame is real but it is not the cause, which sits one line above it in the message. READ THE ERROR MESSAGE, NOT THE TOP OF THE STACK: the stack names who noticed, the message names what happened. CONSEQUENCE BEYOND CI, and it is the important half: this is a statement about the IMAGE, not about our test harness, so the production deployment must not move to SQL Server 2025 either. The disposition of #135 - close it, or leave it open for dependabot to re-raise when a working image ships - is the operator's, because DEC-072 d1 said sweep everything and this one cannot be swept.

#137 AND #261 ARE SUPERSEDED BY A COMBINED PULL REQUEST, #307. The CI log gives the reason exactly: @vitest/coverage-v8 pins an exact peer on its matching vitest, so 'npm error peer vitest@3.2.6 from @vitest/coverage-v8@3.2.6' when vitest alone is bumped, and the mirror failure when coverage-v8 alone is bumped. NEITHER CAN EVER GO GREEN ALONE and GitHub cannot merge two pull requests atomically, so the pair needed one commit. DW-078 predicted this in its own text; the log is the evidence rather than the inference. Both resolve to 4.1.11 under ^4.1.10 and move together. Verified by READING THE REGENERATED LOCKFILE rather than trusting npm's output, which printed 'up to date in 22s' even though the lockfile did change; and the lockfile's alarming shape - plus 534, minus 2288 - was checked rather than accepted as plausible: all 34 declared dependencies still resolve, so the shrinkage is vitest 4 shedding its esbuild-era tree.

FOUR INSTRUMENT FAILURES, ALL MINE, ALL IN ONE SWEEP. (1) The first poller used a read-from-herestring over multi-line python and silently fell back to its default, reporting total=0 for thirty minutes while both pull requests were fully green. IT FAILED SAFELY ONLY BECAUSE OF THE DISCOVERY GUARD: the loop required at least nine checks before declaring completion, so a parser returning zero produced a loud false-FAIL instead of a clean pass over an empty set. Written with the obvious predicate - pending equals zero - a broken parser would have reported ALL COMPLETE having examined nothing. That is trap 31 and DEF-078's healthcheck, and the guard is the entire reason it broke in the safe direction. (2) The replacement poller's reporting field was still wrong: an IN_PROGRESS check carries conclusion as an EMPTY STRING, not null, and my predicate excluded None but not '', so every running check was labelled failing. Note which half broke - the completion logic keyed on status and was correct, only the human-readable field lied. CONTROLS MUST DETECT AND TELL, AND THE TELL HALF IS THE UNTESTED ONE. (3) Extracting a run id with grep -oE '[0-9]+' | head -1 returned 911, taken from the OWNER NAME A-H-911 rather than the URL's run segment; a 404 caught it, but a numeric match that happened to be a valid run id would have silently read another job's log. (4) A background command chain reported exit 0 because its LAST command succeeded, masking an npm EBUSY failure - trap 23b's lesson generalised from pipes to chains. THE COMMON SHAPE ACROSS ALL FOUR: each instrument reported confidently about something it had not actually examined, and only the ones carrying an explicit floor or an external contradiction were caught.

SELF-INFLICTED AND DISCLOSED: npm ci unlinks node_modules before reinstalling and hit EPERM on a locked rolldown native binary partway through, leaving the local node_modules gutted at 35 entries. The repository is untouched - node_modules is gitignored, and git status showed only the two intended package files - and CI is unaffected, but the local checkout cannot run the frontend suite until the lock clears. Recorded rather than quietly repaired.

In a batch merge, #135's failure would have surfaced later as an unrelated-looking integration-test flake, and #307's as a coverage regression that appeared 'sometime last week' across twenty files with no obvious cause.

BLOCKER ONE - #135, AND IT REACHES PRODUCTION. Re-run fresh rather than trusted, because a stale red is exactly as uninformative as a stale green. It fails identically: SearchProvidersFtsTests - the only place any FREETEXT branch executes - dies because the container never starts, with '/opt/mssql/bin/sqlservr: error while loading shared libraries: liblber-2.5.so.0' and exit 127. What fails is ADR-0016's per-file coverage gate over roughly twenty files that are BYTE-IDENTICAL TO main, where main is green at 95 percent or better. The branch changes two lines of package.json plus the lockfile and no source file at all, verified by git diff against origin/main. So coverage-v8 v4 counts lines differently - trap 2 at scale, a measurement indicting known-good code because the instrument changed. Merging it would silently alter what a governance threshold MEASURES while leaving the number alone, so DW-082 carries it and explicitly forbids the tempting fix of lowering the threshold.

INSTRUMENT SCORECARD FOR THE WHOLE SWEEP, because five of my own tools failed and the pattern is uniform. Three pollers broke: the first and third both fell through to their defaults and reported zero checks, and the second labelled every IN_PROGRESS check as failing because a running check carries conclusion as an EMPTY STRING rather than null. A run-id regex returned 911 out of the owner name A-H-911. A background command chain reported exit 0 from its last command while npm had failed inside it. THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE POLLER FAMILY IS AN ENVIRONMENT FACT, NOT A LOGIC ERROR, WHICH IS WHY RE-READING THE LOGIC NEVER FOUND IT: multi-line python inside a command substitution inside a heredoc-written bash script fails silently in this Git Bash; only one single-line python -c per metric works. AND THE DISCOVERY GUARD SAVED IT THREE TIMES: because each loop required at least nine checks before declaring completion, a parser returning zero produced a loud false-FAIL. Written with the obvious predicate - pending equals zero - every one of those breakages would have reported ALL COMPLETE having examined nothing, and I would have merged on an empty set. That is trap 31 paying out three times in one afternoon, in my own instruments, in the session where I recorded the rule twice.

ONE MORE CHECK THAT HAD THE WRONG SUBJECT: resolving #307's conflict, I spot-checked that #259's bumps survived by reading react-router-dom, react-query, typescript and jest-dom - none of which #259 touched. Its six were marked, user-event, types-node, axe-core, oxlint and vite. CORRECTION TO PE-605 AND TO DW-078's ROW - I CONCLUDED THAT #135's FAILURE WAS IN MICROSOFT'S IMAGE AND THAT PRODUCTION MUST NOT MOVE TO SQL SERVER 2025. BOTH HALVES ARE WRONG, AND THE REASONING THAT PRODUCED THEM IS LL-009 VERBATIM.

WHAT I CLAIMED AND WHY IT LOOKED SOLID: SearchProvidersFtsTests failed under Testcontainers, and the e2e job failed identically under plain docker-compose, with the same message - sqlservr cannot load liblber-2.5.so.0, exit 127. I read that as two INDEPENDENT execution paths agreeing, and concluded the fault lay in the base image rather than our harness. THE TWO PATHS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT. Both build deploy/Dockerfile.sqlserver. The thing under test was identical in both; only the orchestration differed, and orchestration is not the variable that mattered. TWO INSTRUMENTS AGREEING IS ONE INSTRUMENT WHEN THEY SHARE A MECHANISM - which is LL-009, a lesson I quoted earlier in this same session before walking into it, because 'different runner, different orchestrator' FEELS like independence.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, MEASURED. The pristine images are each internally consistent: running ldd against /opt/mssql/bin/sqlservr inside both reports NOTHING missing. mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest is Ubuntu 22.04 and ships liblber-2.5.so.0; mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2025-latest is Ubuntu 24.04 and ships liblber.so.2, because OpenLDAP moved from 2.5 to 2.6 and the soname changed. NEITHER IMAGE IS BROKEN. The probe ran with docker run --rm, no volume mounts and no compose, so the five populated ACMP volumes were structurally unreachable rather than merely avoided; they were enumerated before the run and are unchanged.

DW-082 ANSWERED BY EXPERIMENT, AND THE ANSWER REVERSES THE FRAMING: coverage-v8 v4 IS THE MORE HONEST COUNTER, AND THE TWENTY 'REGRESSED' FILES WERE NEVER PROPERLY COVERED. Run exactly as the row's cheapest-first-step specified - same source, same test file, same three passing tests, coverage under v3 then v4, over src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx because at 55 lines it is hand-countable. Executed in a container rather than on the host, because six orphaned vite dev servers hold rolldown's native binary open and npm ci cannot complete there.

RESULT: v3 says 100% lines with nothing uncovered. v4 says 90% lines and names exactly ONE line, 30. Line 30 is a Button whose onClick is an inline arrow calling window.location.reload(). The tests render the fallback, so that JSX genuinely executes; the third test clicks the OTHER button, go-to-dashboard, on line 31. NOTHING EVER CLICKS RELOAD. The line partially executed - element created, callback never invoked.

THE DECISIVE PART IS THAT BOTH PROVIDERS AGREE ON THE FACTS. Each one's function map records the same uncalled function on line 30; v3 names it onClick, v4 names it anonymous_1. They differ only in where they COUNT it. v3 records zero statements with zero hits, so its line map is clean and line 30 is credited. v4 records statement 3 with zero hits, and that propagates into the line metric. THE DISAGREEMENT IS NOT ABOUT WHAT EXECUTED - it is about whether an uninvoked callback makes its LINE uncovered.

WHY THAT SETTLES IT FOR THIS GATE. ADR-0016's threshold is LINES ONLY; the vitest config says so in as many words - functions and branches are not the basis. Under v3 that renders every untested inline handler INVISIBLE to the gate, because the line is credited for the JSX wrapped around the callback while the callback shows up only in a functions percentage nobody gates on. v4 makes it count. THE UPGRADE DOES NOT LOWER COVERAGE; IT CLOSES A HOLE THAT MADE 'LINES ONLY' WEAKER THAN IT SOUNDS. That is the opposite of what the twenty red files looked like, and it is why the row previously - correctly - forbade lowering the threshold, and why refusing the upgrade on the grounds that v4 miscounts is now unsupported.

THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the one worth carrying: WHEN AN INSTRUMENT CHANGES AND THE NUMBERS GET WORSE, 'THE NEW INSTRUMENT IS BROKEN' AND 'THE OLD INSTRUMENT WAS LYING' PRODUCE IDENTICAL EVIDENCE, and only reading the disputed measurement by hand tells them apart. Trap 2 says a measurement that indicts known-good code is measuring itself - that remains true, but its converse needs saying too: SOMETIMES THE CODE WAS NOT AS GOOD AS THE OLD MEASUREMENT SAID. The discriminator is cheap and it is always the same: shrink the disagreement to one artefact small enough to count by hand.

SCOPE, STATED HONESTLY RATHER THAN GENERALISED: this is PROVEN for one file. The mechanism - inline arrow handlers in JSX - is pervasive in React components and all twenty affected files are components, so the generalisation is highly likely but NOT MEASURED. Each other file must be spot-checked the same way before its tests are written, because a file failing for a different reason would otherwise get the wrong fix.

WHAT IS LEFT IS WORK PLUS ONE OPERATOR CHOICE, recorded in the row: write the missing handler tests and merge #307 once the gate passes honestly; or merge with a deliberately recorded, time-boxed re-baseline naming every file and its number; or stay on vitest 3 and write into ADR-0016 that its lines-only gate cannot see untested inline handlers, which is currently implicit. #307, #261 and #137 stay open meanwhile.

THE BOUND IS DELIBERATELY GENEROUS AND THAT IS A DECISION, NOT AN OVERSIGHT. It covers pull + create + boot + wait strategy, because SqlBackstopFixture's start includes a cold 1.5 GB image pull on a fresh runner. MEASURED, AND IT IS WHY A BOUND ALONE WOULD NOT HAVE SATISFIED THE ROW. Testcontainers' own exception on cancellation is a TimeoutException carrying the message 'The operation has timed out.' - it names no container, no bound and no log. Setting TestcontainersSettings.WaitStrategyTimeout would have stopped the hang and still told nobody what hung, which is the half the cancelled verdict actually cost. This was measured by mutation, not assumed from documentation.

PROVEN BY FORCING IT, as the row required, and NOT by a green run. ContainerStartupTimeoutTests first warms the image with a container that DOES become ready - a positive control that proves the helper does not refuse ordinary starts, and that keeps the cold pull out of the measured window, because a pull inside it would fire the budget before the container existed and the log tail would silently degrade to a placeholder, gutting the second assertion into a pass over nothing. A hollow pass caught before it shipped. The general shape is filed as LL-022 (Proposed): when you WRAP an existing failure to make it legible, the failure is inherited and only the message is yours, so any assertion that would still hold against the unwrapped original is testing the framework rather than the change.

NO DEPENDENCY WAS ADDED. Nothing in package.json or node_modules provides a diff, and the algorithm is thirty lines - an LCS over LINES, which is the right granularity for markdown: a reader asking what changed wants the paragraph or list item, not a character ribbon through a sentence. wikiDiff.ts is its own module so it is testable without the dialog, and it lands at 100% lines AND 100% branches.

BOUNDED ON PURPOSE. The LCS table is O(n times m), fine for a wiki page and hostile for a pasted log, so above DIFF_LINE_LIMIT the comparison is REFUSED with an honest message rather than freezing the tab. The tests exercise the limit from the before side, the after side, and EXACTLY AT it - so the bound is inclusive as written rather than inclusive by accident.

A DEFECT NO TEST IN THE SUITE COULD HAVE SEEN, AND IT IS THE FINDING TO CARRY. Looking at the diff in ARABIC showed it rendering '# Governance charter' as 'Governance charter #', moving a trailing full stop to the front of its line, and pushing '-' list markers to the end. That is bidi reordering of NEUTRAL characters inside an RTL paragraph, and jsdom cannot see it because jsdom does not lay out text. A DIFF THAT DISPLAYS TEXT DIFFERENTLY FROM HOW IT IS STORED IS WORSE THAN NO DIFF - the markdown syntax characters are precisely what the reader is checking, so the view would have been actively misleading in Arabic while passing every test. Fixed with unicode-bidi:plaintext, which takes each LINE's direction from its own first strong character, so an Arabic body reads right-to-left and a markdown line reads left-to-right inside one RTL page. Re-verified after the fix by measurement, not by eye alone: the +/- gutter is a SINGLE column in both directions and the document never scrolls sideways.

THE GENERALISATION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX. white-space:pre preserves WHITESPACE, not character ORDER. Any pre-formatted or code-like surface this app grows - a log viewer, a JSON preview, a config panel - needs the same treatment, and none of them will fail a test if it is missing.

A PRE-EXISTING TEST WAS BRIEFLY BROKEN AND THE FIX WAS TO STOP PERTURBING IT. WHAT I RECOMMENDED, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG. Having found no settings store in the app, I proposed appsettings-backed RetentionOptions with a read-only admin display - reasoning that legal sets retention rarely, so a deploy is an acceptable cadence. THE ARCHITECTURE ALREADY DECIDES THIS AND DECIDES IT DIFFERENTLY. SEC-080 (DOC-011, Audit and Records Management) states the canonical posture and names the home explicitly: 'the Configuration table (16 section 2.15) holds retention settings for legal/compliance to set later'. SEC-103 (DOC-014, Data Architecture) specifies that table: Key NVARCHAR UNIQUE, Value NVARCHAR holding JSON, Scope NVARCHAR, Guid PK, described as 'Externalized app/runtime config (non-secret) + retention settings', with the explicit note that 'Retention is configurable here (no purge v1, NFR-059)' and that secrets stay in the env/secret store and NOT here. Building appsettings-backed options would therefore be an architectural DIVERGENCE requiring a scope-change row, not a cheap satisfaction of the requirement.

THE TABLE DOES NOT EXIST. Verified with a control, because the obvious grep lies here: searching for 'class Configuration' returns many hits and EVERY ONE is an EF entity-type configuration under Persistence/Configurations/ - a naming collision, not the specified table. The control term 'class Stream' resolves to a real domain entity, so the instrument works and the absence is real.

FOUR MORE FACTS THE KEYWORD SWEEP FOUND THAT AN IDENTIFIER SWEEP WOULD NOT HAVE (LL-008 paying out again). (1) SEC-089 lists 'retention policy ENFORCEMENT (Phase 2)' among the background-processing needs - so v1 must not enforce, and the register already says so rather than leaving it to inference. (2) SEC-084's OQ-DATA-004 makes the PERIODS THEMSELVES an open question awaiting legal, so 'configurable' cannot mean shipping values; it means shipping the mechanism that can hold them. (3) SEC-077 classifies a 'retention/immutability config change' as a PRIVILEGED ACTION THAT MUST BE AUDITED - so writing a retention setting has to emit an AuditEvent, which no part of the row mentions. (4) SEC-080 also carries LEGAL HOLD, marked '[unverified - confirm hold workflow with legal]' and overriding any future purge; OQ-DATA-003 makes the hold workflow itself an open question.

SO THE HONEST SIZE IS A NEW CROSS-CUTTING TABLE plus a migration, a read/write path, authorization, an audit event on write, and an admin surface with NO design reference (the Administration reference draws exactly five tabs and the app implements those five, so a retention surface is a no-reference composition that must be flagged as one). That is a slice, not an item - and it is the FIFTH row in SL-033 whose sizing was wrong, in a fifth distinct way: not a mis-summary, not a correction that held, not a source comment, not a remedy too small, but a single word ('configurable') covering a subsystem the architecture had already specified and nobody had built.

NOT BUILT, DELIBERATELY. Choosing between the specified Configuration table and any cheaper substitute is a SCOPE decision, which is the operator's alone, and proceeding on my earlier recommendation would have produced work that had to be torn out. DEC-013 is Approved canon here ('keep all records, no auto-purge in v1; retention configurable', reopen only via a new ADR), so nothing about the POSTURE is in question - only the mechanism and its size.

DEC-083 d2 required both alpine and distroless spiked with MEASURED findings; five candidate .NET 10 aspnet bases were probed, and the culture behaviour was established by publishing ONE binary and running it unchanged on all five, so any difference is the base and not the app. THE MEASUREMENTS. Debian 10.0 (current): 229 MB, ICU 74.2, shell, app user, 0 critical / 0 high / 26 medium / 13 low, ar-SA renders Hijri with Arabic-Indic separators. 10.0-alpine: 120 MB, NO ICU, 0/2/6/12, every culture operation THROWS. 10.0-alpine-extra: 159 MB, ICU 78.1, 0/2/6/12, ar-SA renders GREGORIAN with ASCII separators. 10.0-noble-chiseled: 123 MB, NO ICU, NO SHELL, 0/0/4/6, every culture operation THROWS. 10.0-noble-chiseled-extra: 162 MB, ICU 74.2, NO SHELL, 0/0/4/7, ar-SA output BYTE-IDENTICAL to Debian. FALSIFIED CLAIM ONE, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT: the package said a naive minimal-base move would not degrade Arabic but would THROW at runtime after compiling and unit-testing perfectly. Measured, that is only half right and the wrong half is the dangerous one. A no-ICU image does NOT abort at startup - the app starts, exits 0, and silently enters globalization-invariant mode, throwing only when a non-invariant culture is TOUCHED. And ACMP's API touches none: all 10 CultureInfo usages in src are InvariantCulture, and RequestLocalization, SupportedCultures, IStringLocalizer, Accept-Language, new CultureInfo and .resx all return ZERO across 693 .cs files. So a naive move to plain chiseled or alpine would very likely NOT throw for ACMP today. It would ship a container in which the first piece of server-side culture-aware code ever written throws in Arabic, with nothing failing in between. The trap is armed and invisible rather than loud. FALSIFIED CLAIM TWO: the risk was framed as musl versus glibc. The measured risk that actually bites is the ICU VERSION, which is orthogonal to musl. alpine-extra ships ICU 78.1 against Debian's 74.2, and CLDR changed ar-SA's default calendar in that range, so the SAME binary renders 19 rabi al-awwal 1448 on Debian and 1 September 2026 on alpine-extra. No exception, no log line, different output, Arabic only. A size-and-CVE comparison would never have surfaced it. FALSIFIED CLAIM THREE: DEC-083 d2 asked what a no-ICU base implies for FREETEXT and LCID 1025. Measured: nothing. Every LCID 1025 reference is an EF migration creating a full-text index with LANGUAGE 1025, which SQL Server executes inside the sqlserver-fts container - an image NFR-054 excludes and this change does not touch. Arabic word-breaking cannot be affected by the api base. AN INSTRUMENT FAILURE WORTH KEEPING: the probe printed invariant-mode off on the very images where the runtime WAS in invariant mode, because AppContext.TryGetSwitch reports the explicit SWITCH and not the EFFECTIVE mode - the runtime falls back to invariant when ICU is absent without setting it. The behavioural probe is what gave the true answer; the flag would have said everything was fine. Separately a PowerShell tar probe reported NO ICU for chiseled-extra whose behaviour proved otherwise, and the bash form measured ICU 74.2 - a verifier disagreeing with observed behaviour is the verifier being wrong, and it was not reported until the two agreed. THE RECOMMENDATION PUT TO THE OPERATOR IS 10.0-noble-chiseled-extra: NFR-054's equivalent distroless, 162 MB against 229, medium CVEs 26 to 4 and low 13 to 7 with no highs where both alpine variants carry two, glibc so the musl and native-interop risk disappears, and ICU 74.2 so Arabic output is provably unchanged. ⭐⭐ **THE TRIGGER, DERIVED FROM THE CONTROL FLOW RATHER THAN GUESSED, AND IT EXPLAINS THE INTERMITTENCY EXACTLY.** `ParseErrorNoContent` first tries two branches that call `ParseWellKnownErrorNoContent`, which THROWS the typed exception. Both branches key on the same five statuses: **Forbidden, BadRequest, NotFound, MethodNotAllowed, NotImplemented**. So:
• **The normal case never reaches the bug.** A `StatObject` miss — absent object or absent bucket — returns **404**, which is well-known, so the SDK throws `ObjectNotFoundException` / `BucketNotFoundException` and `MinioFileStore.ExistsAsync` catches it and returns `false`. That is why this test has passed on every run but one.
• **A 5xx reaches it.** A status outside those five and not `0` — 500, 502, **503**, 504 — with an **empty body** and no client-side transport exception (`response.Exception == null`) falls past both branches, past the `StatusCode == 0` guard, and onto `response.Exception.GetType()`. **`NullReferenceException`**, where the SDK's own next line intended to throw a descriptive `InternalClientException`.
• **`StatObject` is a HEAD request**, so its error responses carry no body by construction — which is why this adapter's read probe is the place it surfaces.

✅ **SO THE ANSWER TO *why then and not three minutes earlier* IS: MinIO ANSWERED A HEAD WITH A TRANSIENT 5xx.** That is a normal, protocol-defined condition for an object store under load, and the SDK converts it into an uninformative NRE instead of the error it meant to raise. ⛔ **`DEF-108`'s and `DEF-121`'s trigger was never diagnosed; this one is.** The two should not be reasoned about together beyond their shared PR-run/merge-run shape.

⚠⚠ **THE FOUR LOCAL GREENS ARGUE FOR NOTHING AND ARE RECORDED AS SUCH (`LL-018`).** `MinioFileStoreTests` was run 4 times locally against a real pinned MinIO container and passed every time — but each run used `--filter`, so `Acmp.Api.Tests` and the other projects were NOT running in parallel. **The load condition the hypothesis names was absent from the samples taken to test it**, which makes them evidence about a different situation. A superficially different instrument is not an independent one.

⛔⛔ **WHAT THIS RULES OUT, WHICH IS THE PRACTICAL VALUE.** (a) **Widening `ExistsAsync`'s catch is now definitively wrong**, not merely distasteful: the NRE means *the store returned an error I could not parse*, and on a 5xx that is emphatically not *the object is absent*. (b) **Upgrading the SDK does not fix it** — measured on `7.0.0`. (c) A bare re-run would have produced a green and taught nothing, and the register would still say *environmental, undiagnosed*.

⚠ **NO CODE HAS BEEN CHANGED.** The operator's instruction was to investigate before changing anything, and the remedy is a fresh decision: a bounded retry on the read probe (a 5xx is protocol-defined as retryable, so this is the specified handling rather than an `LL-035` probability-fudge), or wrapping the SDK's NRE into a diagnostic naming bucket, object and status, or both. **That is scoped work nobody has planned, and it is being put to the operator.**

Twenty factories were built, exercised, disposed and held only by WeakReference; after a forced full GC, 20 OF 20 WERE STILL ALIVE, with 141 MB retained. The working seam needs no live provider at all: at disposal, build a fresh options-only DbContext per store NAME and call Database.EnsureDeleted(), because EF deletes an InMemory store by name and any options-only context type will do. StartOrFailFastAsync's catch previously carried a 'when (ex is TimeoutException or OperationCanceledException && cts.IsCancellationRequested)' filter, so a container that CRASHED went straight through it uncaught - which is exactly what DEF-121's occurrence did. The filter is now inside the catch instead of on it, so every start failure captures first and the original exception is then rethrown unwrapped. That last part is deliberate and is why the capture never wraps: DEF-121's signature is a ContainerNotRunningException and DEF-109's is a TaskCanceledException in a different suite, and the register discriminates the two families on exactly that. docker cp rather than IContainer.ReadFileAsync because the core file's NAME is timestamped and cannot be requested by path in advance.
